record.paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
record.original_question: When one uses a closed temporal-network model for analytic or computational tractability even though the real population interacts with individuals outside the modeled network, can those external interactions be incorporated statistically in a way that still yields useful epidemic-threshold calculations?

evidence.quote: And, when we require closed models for analytic or computational tractability, can we account statistically for assumed interactions with individuals external to the network?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a population modeled by a temporal contact network: a vertex set $V$ together with a time-indexed family of edge sets $\{E(t)\}_{t \in T}$, encoding which pairs of individuals are in contact at each time. On this network, run a stochastic compartmental epidemic process (e.g., SIS or SIR) with infection rate $\beta$ along active edges and recovery rate $\mu$. The epidemic threshold is the critical value of $\beta/\mu$ separating extinction of the infection from a sustained outbreak.

For analytical or computational tractability, one often restricts attention to a closed temporal-network model, in which only contacts among the vertices of $V$ are represented, even though in reality individuals in $V$ also interact with individuals outside $V$. Model these unmodeled external contacts statistically: for instance, augment each vertex $v \in V$ with an independent inhomogeneous external infection process of rate $\lambda_v(t)$ (or, equivalently, attach a random time-varying boundary force of infection drawn from a prescribed distribution, possibly correlated across vertices and time).

The problem is the following: design such a statistical augmentation and a corresponding analytic framework so that one can compute (or rigorously bound) the epidemic threshold of the closed temporal-network model with external forcing, in a way that yields predictions which usefully approximate the threshold of the true open system. Concretely, identify classes of temporal networks and classes of external-interaction statistical models for which the epidemic threshold can be derived in closed form or via a tractable spectral / mean-field calculation, and quantify the error introduced by replacing the open system with the closed-plus-external-forcing surrogate.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in the temporal-networks epidemic-threshold literature. Searches return the original review and related works on threshold computations for closed temporal-network models (spectral, contact-based, switching, modular formulations), but no work that systematically incorporates statistical models of external (off-network) interactions into a tractable threshold calculation. The question therefore appears to remain open.
